8. Respondent No.2, who, at one point of time, has put the criminal machinery into motion, by lodging the 4 ( 2024:HHC:11109 ) FIR, in question, against the petitioner, today, appeared, before this Court and deposed that due to some misunderstanding, she had lodged the FIR, in question,

9. According to respondent No.2, now, with the intervention of the respectables of the society and in order to maintain their future cordial relations, the matter has been compromised with the petitioner, vide compromise deed Annexure P3.
The compromise has been effected between with the petitioner out of her free will, consent and without any pressure upon her.
10. On the basis of the above facts, respondent No.2, has no objection, in case the petition is allowed, as prayed for.
11. Similar type of statement has also been made by the petitioner, on oath.

In this case, the criminal machinery was put into motion, by respondent No.2, by lodging the FIR, in question, however, when, appeared before this Court, she has exonerated the petitioner from the allegations, by deposing, on oath, that due to some misunderstanding, she had lodged the FIR,

14. Once, the person, who had put the criminal machinery into motion, has exonerated the petitioner from the allegations, in such situation, the chances of success of prosecution case, against the petitioner, are not so bright.
